newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spanish businessmen see economy improving, survey.
newsitem.headline: Spanish businessmen see economy improving, survey.

text.p: The conservative Spanish Popular Party government is doing a good job managing the economy, which should improve in the next 12 months, according to a new survey of business conditions published on Sunday.

Nine out of 10 businessmen surveyed said the economy would pick up in the next 12 months, and they applauded the government's role - with 58.7 percent categorising its performance as good or very good.
A sharp reduction in inflation, a stable exchange rate, and efforts to meet criteria for the launch of Europe's common currency were considered the government's key accomplishments.

The Popular Party, which took over the government last spring after 13 years of Socialist rule, has presided over a sharp drop in inflation, the stabilisation of the peseta after a series of devaluations, and has undertaken belt-tightening and liberalisation measures.

The quarterly survey of 247 businesses, which together represent assets or annual sales of 35 trillion pesetas, was carried out in January and compiled in the following weeks by Coopers & Lybrand for Spanish newspaper El Pais.

The businessmen polled welcomed the government's firm commitment to join Europe's single currency. Not one of those surveyed disagreed with the objective and 44 percent said the government should do whatever was necessary to achieve it.
The government's key challenges were labour reform, a reduction in expenditure and in unemployment and fiscal reform.
Labour and employer representatives are in negotiations on reforms to make Spain's rigid labour market more flexible.

Referring to their own businesses, three-quarters of those polled saw corporate profits rising, while an even larger percentage anticipated increases in sales. Some two-thirds expected their investments to increase.
Service-, transport- and manufacturing-sector businesses were the most optimistic for the coming months. The construction sector was the only one that saw conditions worsening.
